title: 'Zero Political Aspirations': UFC Boss Dana White Rejects Trump's Press Secretary Offer at White House Podium
snippet: UFC CEO Dana White joined President Donald Trump in the White House briefing room on Monday to officially decline an invitation to serve as the administration's next press secretary.
content:
WASHINGTON — Ultimate Fighting Championship CEO Dana White took the podium in the White House briefing room on Monday to address days of wild speculation, officially declining President Donald Trump's offer to serve as the administration's next press secretary.

Standing alongside the 80-year-old commander-in-chief in the James S. Brady Press Briefing Room, White—dressed in a black t-shirt and jacket—made it clear that his future remains in combat sports, not West Wing politics.

"So let me ask you the big question," Trump said to White in front of a packed room of journalists. "Would you like to be press secretary of the United States of America? Or do you just want to stay with this ridiculous UFC? Huh?"

"Thank you for the offer, sir... I do not want to be in politics," White replied.

'A Little Fun' at the Podium

The unusual exchange capped off a weekend of frenzy after Trump posted on social media that he had asked White, a longtime friend, to take on the top communications post, describing the 57-year-old fight promoter as a "violent Fighter and Warrior." The post triggered intense speculation about a potential shift in media strategy, though Trump walked back the comments on Sunday night, claiming he was "only kidding."

Bringing White out to the lectern on Monday, Trump admitted he was just "having a little fun" with the press corps. "He's a great guy," Trump said. "The only problem is he'll talk for a little while and then he's going to beat the hell out of you."

White admitted that the past day had been a whirlwind. "The last 24 hours of my life has been insane," he said, clarifying that while he has "zero political aspirations," he didn't want to publicly address the offer until speaking with the president directly. "I don't tell the president 'no' to anything... I didn't want to be disrespectful and say anything until he said something first."

Vacant Press Office Remains Open

Despite the lighthearted moment, the White House press secretary position remains vacant. The post has been open since Katie Zacharia resigned on Oct. 16 after less than a week in the role. Her predecessor, Karoline Leavitt, stepped down in August after a year and a half on the job.

After White formally passed on the gig, Trump feigned heartbreak. "I am devastated to hear this. Goodbye, everybody," he joked before transitioning the press conference toward heavy policy matters, including conflicts in Ukraine and Iran and ongoing legislative battles on Capitol Hill.
